acceptance: Reproduce or explain the cancellation from the workflow concurrency settings
A verdict-triggered oracle-review run is no longer cancelled by concurrent runs, or a cancelled one is automatically re-run, so a PR with a SHIP verdict is not left BLOCKED
Workflow test or documented proof run on a PR
No weakening of the required oracle-review gate
context: Related failure (PR #3049): oracle-verdict run 38938627249's `post` job failed at its last step, "Rerun the failed synchronize suite for this head". It tried to re-run oracle-review run 38938422659, which predated a close/reopen and could not be retried ("This workflow run cannot be retried"). The success status had already been posted, but the failed job marked the PR "unstable", so the first `make pr-arm` auto-merge attempt failed. The rerun step should skip runs that cannot be retried, or only target runs newer than the latest successful oracle-review for that head. Fix both together.
description: After an oracle success verdict, the oracle-review run triggered by that verdict is often cancelled by a concurrent pull_request (or edited/synchronize) run in the same concurrency group. The cancelled check row leaves the PR BLOCKED until someone manually re-runs that specific run. Seen on #2993, #3006, #3004 and others. The existing automatic re-run after a late verdict does not cover this case.
